maria.g: Opened a docs PR to revise the model-catalog entry and model-card for orion-8b-quant: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/857. Changes: add `seq_len_ceiling` column, note KV-cache eviction differences for quant variants, update benchmark table, and replace streaming SDK snippets with the new async iterator pattern. Need quick review before EOD.

ci-bot: PR preview: https://preview.docs.redwood-inference.com/pr-857 Lint OK, accessibility checks OK, linkcheck: 2 warnings (old anchors under /docs/guides/limits and an external benchmark link).

vikram.s: Thanks. Where are the perf numbers coming from? Please include the perf-runner job id and the exact test harness (seq, batch, hardware). We should avoid publishing p99 from batchy tests.

maria.g: Perf artifacts attached in PR. Summary: perf-runner #4910, baseline: seq=2048, batch_size=1, gpu=NVIDIA-A100-40GB, int8 quant. Measured p50/p90/p99 and aggregate throughput. I'll paste the bowdlerized log here.
```
run_id: 4910
seq: 2048
batch: 1
device: A100-40GB
quant: int8
p50: 16.9 ms
p90: 103 ms
p99: 242 ms
tokens_per_sec: 475
notes: KV cache hit rate ~94% for typical convo length
```

jordan_l: We should add a short migration note for customers who pinned the base slug (orion-8b) so they know to opt into `pin_to_variant: "orion-8b-quant"` in their deployment config. I can draft a one-paragraph blurb in /docs/migration/pinning.

frank: Also scanning the repo: several older examples refer to `orion-8b` in code blocks; I'll do a sweep to make sure the new canonical slug `orion-8b-quant` is used in the catalog and examples. Found one dead external link to a third-party benchmark, will swap to our archived snapshot.

emily.k: For the catalog table: adding `seq_len_ceiling` is good. Can we make the values explicit (e.g., "8k (KV-eviction at 8192)") and include a short footnote that customers on Dedicated may see different eviction behavior depending on memory config?

vikram.s: Agreed. Also add a small CPU-fallback row showing degraded throughput so customers don't assume same perf on CPU. I can re-run a lightweight CPU fallback test and add numbers.

jordan_l: Pushing updated SDK snippets now. Using the new async-stream API in both JS/Python examples and showing `pin_to_variant` usage. Here are the proposed snippets (feel free to use them in the PR):

Python (async iterator):
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
import asyncio

async def main():
    client = AsyncClient()
    async for chunk in client.stream_generate(model=\"orion-8b-quant\", prompt=\"Short summary:\", max_tokens=128, pin_to_variant=\"orion-8b-quant\"):
        print(chunk.text, end=\"\")

asyncio.run(main())
```

TypeScript (for-await-of):
```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'
const client = new Redwood()

async function run() {
  const stream = await client.streamGenerate({ model: 'orion-8b-quant', prompt: 'Short summary:', max_tokens: 128, pin_to_variant: 'orion-8b-quant' })
  for await (const part of stream) {
    process.stdout.write(part.text)
  }
}

run()
```

frank: Snippets look tidy. One small nit: use `pin_to_variant` only in examples where we explicitly discuss migration; otherwise it may confuse new users. Add a brief comment above the snippet.

maria.g: Good point. I'll add a short comment block in the doc explaining when to use `pin_to_variant`. Also adding a changelog entry under the model-card noting the eviction caveat and ceiling.

vikram.s: I re-run the GPU and CPU microbenchmarks and adjusted p99 to 248ms to be conservative; noted baseline seq=2048 and CPU fallback on 16 vCPU yields tokens/s ~52. Updated the PR table accordingly.

emily.k: Looks good to me. Assigning final reviewers: Vikram (perf), Jordan (snippets), Frank (link sweep). If all thumbs by EOD we'll merge. :thumbsup:
